feature: An effect at each click of a recording
summary: A recording's clicks can show a ripple, a pulse or a spotlight on the picture as each click lands, in playback, scrubbing and export alike. Each click is a tick on the clip's bar that you can hide or drag to a better moment.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A recording made in Photonz (it keeps its clicks), or any recording after Add Click at Playhead.

try.do: Click the recording on the canvas, then turn on Clicks at the top of its Properties.
Open Style and pick Ripple, Pulse or Spotlight.
Press Space to play through a click, or scrub across it, and watch the ring spread and fade.
Change Color and Size (Small, Medium, Large) and play the click again.
Right-click a tick on the clip's bar and choose Hide This Click.
Drag another tick left or right to move when its effect plays.
Export the video and check the effect is in the file at the same moments.

evaluate: Does Medium read as a ring round the pointer, or is it too small or too big on your recordings?
Is 400 ms long enough to notice the click, especially for Spotlight?
Are the ticks on the clip's bar easy enough to see and grab, or should they be taller?
Is the top of Properties the place you would look for this setting?
Should the blue accent stay the default colour, or would white or yellow read better on screenshots?
rough: No mock draws click effects, so the layout follows the task's list and Screen Studio's settings rather than a design page.
The effect is drawn where the click falls in the uncropped, unrotated recording, so on a cropped or rotated clip it can land off target.
A ripple near the clip's edge can spill a little past the clip onto whatever is beside it.
Spotlight always dims with black, so the Color row is hidden for it.
The ticks are 3 pt wide and 10 pt tall with a 9 pt grab area. A hidden click keeps a faint tick so it can be shown again.
While a tick is being dragged the canvas does not preview the new moment; the effect moves when you let go.
The walks script the clicks onto the sample recording rather than recording live ones; the earlier recorded-clicks walk covers the recorder itself.
